Fresh native computation. Results are not prescribed in advance.
One broken program, a working city.
An infinite loop receives a bounded execution turn. Other eligible programs keep running. Pause or repair that participant without resetting the whole world.
This creates a real extra BF process, within the sixteen-slot limit. Its source and state appear in the object menu. Industrial cargo stays with its owner.
BF checks capacity, schema and ownership. Objects holding material or unfinished jobs cannot be discarded.


THE CITY IS THE EXAMPLE. BRAINFUCK IS THE EXPERIMENT.
Eight instructions. Programs that cooperate.
Thread makes the programs readable.
The Brainfuck programming language has eight instructions: > < + - . , [ ]. They move a pointer, change a cell, read or write a byte, and loop. The BF kernel implements Thread, a small stack language used for the city's programs.
Build 003 adds resumable processes, bounded message queues and a deterministic scheduler inside BF. Depots, factories, vans, stations and traffic signals run distinct programs. BF also owns inventory, routes, road reservations and construction.
Source is stored and compiled inside BF. Old suspended calls keep their version. New invocations adopt an accepted update. A declared incompatible state/message schema is refused. Freed contexts and version arenas can be reused.
The host executes and draws.
Python emits the initial BF kernel. A generic JavaScript/WebAssembly executor runs its eight instructions. JavaScript carries raw input, stores opaque machine images and draws native output. It does not schedule guest processes, deliver their messages, compile their rules or simulate the city.
Architectural images are graphical assets. Materials, cargo, phases of construction and routes are selected from actual BF output. Smooth movement interpolates only between observed positions. This is logical concurrency in one BF machine, not a full operating system or self-hosting.
Resources are finite: sixteen processes, four messages per mailbox, eight modules and sixteen version arenas. Native work can take seconds; camera movement remains available while it computes.

Export saves the whole machine, including messages and unfinished work. An imported image must match this kernel. Older snapshots need their Build 002 or Build 001 runtime. Import is checked in a new candidate machine before it replaces the current workspace.
